title: Tiltrotor Crew Chief, MV-22 (GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
17.     MOS 6176, Tiltrotor Crew Chief, MV-22 (GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. Tiltrotor Crew Chiefs, MV-22 are flight crew members who,
when assigned to the flight schedule, are responsible to the pilot in command
while in operation of the aircraft and associated mission/weapons systems.
When not assigned to the flight schedule they report to their respective work
center within the maintenance department where they inspect, service,
maintain, and repair power plants, transmissions, drivetrains, fuel systems,
and rotor systems.


                                        3-380                          Enclosure (1)
 3139                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen (no waivers).

            (2) Must pass a rigorous flight physical.

            (3) Must have a five-year term of enlistment.

            (4) Must have a WS-B(+) water survival qualification.

            (5) Must pass the normal color perception test (no waivers).

            (6) Security requirement:   secret security clearance eligibility.

            (7) Volunteer for duties involving flight as an aircraft crewmember.

        (8) Meet the requirements of reference (ah), and (ai) with normal
depth perception.

        (9) Must possess an EL score of 105 or GT score of 105 or MM score of
105 or higher.

        (10) Vision no worse than 20/70 in one eye and 20/100 in the other
with overall vision correctable to 20/20.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Must complete the following course(s):

                (a) Naval Aircrew Member Candidate School Course (N2373C3).

                (b) MV-22 Tiltrotor Crew Chief Osprey Course (M0568H1).

                (c) MV-22 Tiltrotor Marine Enlisted Aircrew Training Course
(M05AFD0).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference(s) (ad) COMNAVAIRFORINST 4790.2, bn) NAVMC 4790, and (bo) NAVMC
3500.14.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
49-1011.

            (2) Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians 49-3011.

            (3) Aircraft Cargo Handling Supervisor 53-1041.

            (4) First-Line Supervisors of Air Crew Members 55-2011.

            (5) Cleaners of Vehicles and Equipment 53-7061.

            (6) Air Crew Members 55-3011.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Helicopter Mechanic, CH-53, 6113.




                                         3-381                         Enclosure (1)
 3139                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



            (2) Helicopter Mechanic, UH/AH-1, 6114.

            (3) Tiltrotor Mechanic, MV-22, 6116.

            (4) Helicopter Crew Chief, CH-53, 6173.

            (5) Helicopter Crew Chief, UH-1, 6174.

            (6) Fixed-Wing Aircraft Mechanic AV-8/TAV-8, 6212.

            (7) Fixed-Wing Aircraft Mechanic KC-130, 6216.

            (8) Fixed-Wing Aircraft Mechanic F-18, 6217.

            (9) Fixed-Wing Aircraft Mechanic F-35, 6218.

            (10) Fixed-Wing Loadmaster, KC-130, 6276.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations.
